sources.entry: Mopidy ⚠ - Extensible music server. Offers a superset of the mpd API, as well as integration with 3rd party services like Spotify, SoundCloud etc. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Python/deb

summary.one_liner: Mopidy is an extensible music server written in Python that plays music from local disk, Spotify, SoundCloud, internet radio and more, controlled by any MPD or web client.
summary.what_it_does: Mopidy is a music server written in Python. It plays audio from local disk, Spotify, SoundCloud, internet radio, and other sources. Playback is controlled from any MPD (Music Player Daemon) or web client on a phone, tablet, or computer. The README describes it as extensible, and the awesome-selfhosted listing notes it offers a superset of the MPD API along with integrations with third-party services. The README gives install instructions only as a pointer to the docs, which cover Debian, Ubuntu, Raspberry Pi OS, Arch Linux, macOS, and manual installation. It also links to a website, documentation, a Discourse forum, a Zulip chat, and an issue tracker.
use_cases: control local music library from phone
play Spotify or SoundCloud on a home audio system
how_to_run: See the installation docs for packages for Debian, Ubuntu, Raspberry Pi OS, Arch Linux, macOS, and manual installation.
notable: Speaks the MPD protocol, so any MPD client can control it
Extensible through extensions for third-party services
Plays local disk, Spotify, SoundCloud, and internet radio
Packaged for several Linux distributions and macOS
caveats: Install steps are only linked to external docs, not given in the README
Some sources (e.g., Spotify, SoundCloud) depend on extensions, which the README does not detail
The awesome-selfhosted listing is marked with a warning symbol, meaning it may have an issue
